name: Majapahit
title: Social Hierarchy of Majapahit: From God-King to Palace Servant
period: 1293–1389 (from Raden Wijaya to the death of Hayam Wuruk)

tiers.name: The king
tiers.you: You are hailed as the universal ruler and a living god, and once a year envoys from every land that pays you tax or tribute come to your court to honour you.
tiers.kid: The king of Majapahit was seen as a living god, and once a year people from many islands came to bring him tribute.
tiers.rise: The throne passed within the house of Raden Wijaya, and a woman could hold it: when Jayanegara was murdered in 1328, childless, the Queen Grandmother Gayatri Rajapatni, who had become a Buddhist nun, set her daughter Tribhuwana on it. After Hayam Wuruk died in 1389, his son-in-law and his son by a concubine fought over it in the Regreg War of 1405–1406.
tiers.why: The king was the paramount ruler: as chakravartin he was considered the universal ruler and believed to be a living god on earth, regarded as the incarnation of Shiva, Vishnu and the Buddha at once, and held the…

tiers.name: Royal kin and provincial lords
tiers.you: You are a close relative of the king and rule a province of east Java as its Bhre, collecting its taxes and sending tribute to the capital each year; you may sit among the seven elders who advise the king.
tiers.kid: The king’s close relatives ruled the provinces of Java and helped him make big decisions.
tiers.rise: Royal birth or marriage brought the rank, and its members fought for more. Bhre Wirabhumi, Hayam Wuruk’s son by a concubine, claimed the throne against Vikramavardhana and was caught and beheaded in the Regreg War; the council then sentenced to death the man who had beheaded him.
tiers.why: The title Bhre, “duke or duchess”, marked the highest position below the monarch.

tiers.name: Ministers, officials and nobles
tiers.term: Rakryan Mantri ri Pakira-kiran, Rakryan Mapatih, Patih Hamangkubhumi, akuwu
tiers.you: You sit on the king’s board of ministers, live in quarters outside the palace, and ride out to hunt with a gold-inlaid kris; but a minister who breaks the law may pay with his life.
tiers.kid: Ministers helped the king run Majapahit, and the greatest of them, Gajah Mada, swore to unite the islands.
tiers.rise: Service could raise a man far. Gajah Mada, who saved Jayanegara with his Bhayangkara guard during the Kuti rebellion of 1319, was promoted to high office and in 1336 became mahapatih; Adityawarman, Jayanegara’s cousin, rose to be a senior minister. Office could also end in death: Halayudha, who had plotted against his rivals at court, was sentenced to death, and the minister Demung Sora was sentenced to death for killing Mahisa Anabrang.
tiers.why: Royal edicts passed from the king to the high officials and on to their subordinates.

tiers.name: Priests and religious teachers
tiers.you: You study under a mahāresi in a Kadewaguruan high in the hills, far from the towns, learning the rites you may one day perform at court.
tiers.kid: Priests of Shiva and of the Buddha led the kingdom’s ceremonies, and students learned from teachers in schools high in the hills.
tiers.rise: Learning passed through the households of brahmana families and the Kadewaguruan, schools set in quiet forests or on hills and mountains far from habitation, each led by a mahāresi, a high priest also called dewaguru. Royalty too could enter religious life, as Gayatri Rajapatni did when she became a Buddhist nun.
tiers.why: Religion had officials of its own.

tiers.name: Professional soldiers
tiers.you: You are a full-time soldier of the king, paid in gold and armoured in scales, and you may sail on a great jong to bring a rebellious vassal to heel.
tiers.kid: Majapahit had a paid army of 30,000 soldiers and great ships called jongs that carried them across the sea.
tiers.rise: A soldier could rise far: Gajah Mada led the Bhayangkara guard that saved Jayanegara in 1319 and became prime minister. Many died far from home in the kingdom’s wars: in southern Borneo the dead were burned at Tambak Wasi in 1358, and surviving soldiers, sailors and metalsmiths settled in Amuntai, Alabio and Nagara.
tiers.why: The army had two kinds of men: prajurit, professional soldiers, and levies taken from the peasants.

tiers.name: Foreign merchants
tiers.you: You are a Muslim merchant settled in the port of Tuban, paying the special tax laid on foreigners who stay and do business in Java, while the spices of Maluku pass through your hands.
tiers.kid: Traders from China, India, Arabia and nearby islands came to Majapahit’s ports to buy and sell spices.
tiers.rise: Foreigners rose by trade and by the king’s favour: Ma Huan counted seven or eight leaders among the foreign families of the capital who served the king. In the 15th century King Kertabhumi gave Muslim merchants trading rights on the north coast in return for their loyalty, and the coastal power of Demak that grew from them overthrew the kingdom in 1527.
tiers.why: The fame of the king, the Nagarakretagama says, drew foreign merchants from far and wide: Indians, Khmers, Siamese and Chinese among them.

tiers.name: Artisans and traders
tiers.you: You are a goldsmith, paid in Chinese copper coins, and you keep your savings in a clay money box shaped like a wild boar.
tiers.kid: Craftspeople in Majapahit made gold jewellery, clay pots and money boxes shaped like wild boars.
tiers.rise: Court artisans worked for the royal house, preparing the great ceremonies of the court. Others were carried far by the kingdom’s wars, as the metalsmiths who settled in Borneo after the campaign of 1358; and when Majapahit fell, many artisans, with courtiers and priests, fled east to Bali.
tiers.why: Inscriptions of the period mention a large number of occupations, from gold and silversmiths to drink vendors and butchers, and the share of people earning an income from work other than farming seems to have grown.

tiers.name: Rice farmers
tiers.you: You grow rice in a village of east Java and harvest it twice a year, keep your family’s goods in a brick shed and sleep on top of it, and march bare-chested with a spear when the levy is called.
tiers.kid: Most people in Majapahit were rice farmers, and their rich fields gave two harvests a year.
tiers.rise: Levies were led by the warrior and noble castes and fought far from home, and some never came back: Javanese soldiers who survived the Borneo war settled where they had fought. The sources used here give no other path out of the village.

tiers.name: Servants of the palace and great households
tiers.you: You live in a row of servants’ houses on the terraces of the royal compound, inside the red brick walls of the king’s palace.
tiers.kid: Servants lived in rows of houses inside the palace walls and worked for the royal family.
tiers.rise: How people entered service, and whether they could leave it, is not recorded in the sources used here.
tiers.why: The royal compound at Trowulan, walled in red brick, held more than the king and his court: at the south end of its first courtyard a gate led to rows of houses set on terraces, where the palace servants lived.
